text:
The Islanders lost 4-3 in overtime in Winnipeg on Thursday, which still stretched their point streak to six games (3-0-3). The bigger worry came after: coach Pete DeBoer said there was no update on Ryan Pulock and that he'll have to see doctors, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner.

At 10-6-5, the record runs ahead of the play. New York gets 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our points from the play come to 19.5 against their 25. The cushion is Ilya Sorokin and company: the Islanders have allowed 14.1 fewer goals than expected, and Sorokin has saved 5.2 above expected over his last five starts.

The other story is Matthew Schaefer, the second-year defenseman with 14 points in his last 10 who is making history at a pace people keep writing about. His pair with Logan Stanley has 54% of the chances. Up front, Bo Horvat, Kyle Palmieri and Simon Holmstrom are the line that creates, at 57%, and Holmstrom has made the most of his chances with his first NHL hat trick against Anaheim.

If Pulock misses time, it hurts a defense that already gives up a lot: his pair with Adam Pelech was the team's shutdown unit by goals, 6-1. The Islanders are 37% to make the playoffs by our odds. What we'd watch is the shot share in the next stretch. A team this reliant on its goalie needs Sorokin to stay this good, and that's a hard thing to bank on.
headline: The Islanders are leaning on Sorokin and Schaefer
